title: A Story with Two Beginnings
title_ja: 二つの始まりを持つ物語
fact_notes: オリジナル教材。人物、出来事は架空の例であり、実在の調査や実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A reader who encounters a character for the first time may form an impression that influences the way later events in a story are interpreted.
sentences.ja: 初めて登場人物に出会う読者は後の出来事の解釈に影響する印象を形成し得る。

sentences.en: A writer can therefore change the experience of reading a story without altering the events that the characters eventually experience.
sentences.ja: そこで作家は登場人物が最終的に経験する出来事を変えずに読書体験を変えられる。

sentences.en: One way of doing so is to modify the order in which readers receive information about the characters and their circumstances.
sentences.ja: 一つの方法は登場人物と事情について読者が情報を受け取る順序を変えることだ。

sentences.en: A classroom writing exercise provides an opportunity to explore this relationship between narrative order and interpretation.
sentences.ja: 教室の作文活動は物語の順序と解釈の関係を探る機会を提供する。

sentences.en: Two students prepare different versions of an imaginary story about a traveler who unexpectedly leaves a group of friends during an important journey.
sentences.ja: 二人の生徒は重要な旅の途中で予想外に友人グループから離れる旅行者の架空物語を異なる版で用意する。

sentences.en: The first version begins with the moment of departure, encouraging readers to wonder why the character has apparently abandoned the others.
sentences.ja: 第一版は出発の瞬間に始まり、人物が一見他の人を見捨てた理由を読者に考えさせる。

sentences.en: The second version initially describes a message that the traveler received earlier, explaining that someone nearby urgently needed help.
sentences.ja: 第二版は当初、旅行者が以前受け取ったメッセージを記述し近くの誰かが緊急に助けを必要としていたと説明する。

sentences.en: Both versions eventually provide the same basic information, although they reveal it at different points in the narrative.
sentences.ja: 両版は最終的に同じ基本情報を提供するが物語の異なる箇所で明らかにする。

sentences.en: During a class discussion, students compare the questions that each opening might encourage readers to ask.
sentences.ja: 授業の議論で各冒頭が読者に問わせるかもしれない問いを比較する。

sentences.en: A reader of the first version might initially question the traveler's loyalty, whereas a reader of the second might be concerned about the consequences of the unexpected message.
sentences.ja: 第一版の読者は旅行者の忠誠を最初疑い、第二版の読者は予想外のメッセージの影響を心配するかもしれない。

sentences.en: The class recognizes that these reactions are possible interpretations rather than guaranteed responses from every actual reader.
sentences.ja: これら反応は全実読者の保証された返答でなく可能な解釈と認識する。

sentences.en: They also examine how the later explanation might encourage a reader to reconsider an earlier judgment.
sentences.ja: 後の説明が以前の判断を再考するよう読者を促す様子も調べる。

sentences.en: The teacher distinguishes the sequence of events within the imagined world from the order in which those events are presented to readers.
sentences.ja: 教師は仮想世界内の出来事の順序と読者への提示順序を区別する。

sentences.en: Students can preserve the first sequence while experimenting with the second.
sentences.ja: 生徒は第一の順序を維持しながら第二を試せる。

sentences.en: However, changing the presentation order may require adjustments to descriptions so that readers can follow the relationships between events.
sentences.ja: しかし提示順の変更には出来事間の関係を読者が追えるよう記述の調整が必要かもしれない。

sentences.en: The activity encourages students to develop intentional choices about which information should be revealed and when it should become available.
sentences.ja: 活動はどの情報を公開し、いつ利用可能にするか意図的な選択を発展させるよう促す。

sentences.en: A story does not simply communicate a collection of events.
sentences.ja: 物語は単に出来事の集合を伝えるのではない。

sentences.en: It creates an experience in which readers encounter information over time and gradually form or revise their understanding.
sentences.ja: 読者が時間とともに情報に出会い徐々に理解を形成・修正する経験を作る。

sentences.en: The two versions illustrate how narrative structure can influence a reader's attention without necessarily changing the facts of the imagined world.
sentences.ja: 二版は物語構造が仮想世界の事実を必ずしも変えず読者の注意に影響することを示す。

sentences.en: Learning to recognize that structure can make both reading and writing more thoughtful activities.
sentences.ja: その構造を認識する学びは読書と作文をより思慮深い活動にし得る。

vocabulary.definition: relating to the telling of a story
giving someone a reason to act
modifications made to suit a situation
in a way that must occur

questions.prompt: How can a writer alter the reading experience without changing events?
options: By removing every character from the story.
By making all events happen simultaneously.
By changing the order in which information is presented.
By preventing readers from forming any impression.

questions.prompt: What relationship does the exercise explore?
How does the first version begin?
options: With the end of the journey.
With an explanation of the classroom activity.

questions.prompt: What does the second version explain earlier?
options: The traveler was never with friends.
The friends did not know the traveler.

questions.prompt: Why might readers of the two versions ask different questions?
options: The events themselves are completely unrelated.
Only one version has a character.
They receive important information in different orders.
Both versions reveal all information immediately.

questions.prompt: Why avoid predicting identical reactions from every reader?
options: Every story has only one possible interpretation.
A fictional example proves universal outcomes.

questions.prompt: What distinction does the teacher make?
Why might changing presentation order require other revisions?
options: Every change must remove all earlier events.
Readers still need to understand relationships between events.
Readers must be told the final answer immediately.
questions.explanation_ja: 関係を理解できるように。

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the main argument?
options: The chronological order is the only possible way to tell a story.
Narrative order shapes the reader's understanding even when the story's events remain the same.
Storytelling is merely a list of facts.
questions.explanation_ja: 提示順序と読者の理解。

grammar.focus: whereas a reader of the second

paraphrases.source: A writer can therefore change the experience of reading a story without altering the events that the characters eventually experience.
paraphrases.rewrite: The writer can change the reading experience while keeping the events unchanged.

paraphrases.source: The first version begins with the moment of departure, encouraging readers to wonder why the character has apparently abandoned the others.
paraphrases.rewrite: The opening invites readers to question the reason for the traveler's departure.

paraphrases.source: A reader of the first version might initially question the traveler's loyalty, whereas a reader of the second might be concerned about the consequences of the unexpected message.
paraphrases.rewrite: The first opening may raise doubts about loyalty, while the second raises concern about the message.

paraphrases.source: However, changing the presentation order may require adjustments to descriptions so that readers can follow the relationships between events.
paraphrases.rewrite: Descriptions may need adjustment to help readers follow the sequence of events.
